draft.title: The Roman Republic
card: The Romans drove out their last king, according to tradition in 509 BCE. They set up a republic, a state led by elected officials instead of a king.
two officials elected each year to lead Rome. Having two meant neither could rule alone, and each term lasted one year.
a council of powerful men who advised the consuls and had great influence over laws, money and war.
Patricians were wealthy families who held most of the power. Plebeians were ordinary citizens who had little say at first, and they pushed for a share of power.
draft.remember: The Republic shared power among elected officials and the Senate, but patricians held most of it.

a.q: Why did the Romans elect two consuls each year instead of one?
opts: So that no single man could rule alone
So that one consul could lead the army only
So that patricians and plebeians each had a king
So that the Senate would not be needed
a.why: Two consuls had to share power, and their terms lasted only a year, so no one could rule like a king. The Senate was still needed, because it advised the consuls and influenced laws, money and war.
a.clue: Think about what the Romans wanted to avoid after the kings.

b.q: In the early Republic, Marcus is a plebeian who wants a say in how Rome is run. What was his position?
opts: He had little power and could push for a share
He was a consul because he was a citizen
He sat in the Senate as a member of a royal family
He held most of the power as a patrician
b.why: Plebeians were ordinary citizens with little say at first, and they pushed for a share of power. Patricians, not plebeians, held most of the power.
b.clue: Which group held most power at first?

a.best: So that no single man could rule alone

b.best: He had little power and could push for a share

problems.detail: Patricians were a hereditary class defined by birth into certain old families, not simply 'wealthy families'. Some plebeians were wealthy too. Saying patricians were noble or old aristocratic families by birth would be more accurate.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer, and the explanations match the card. The only issue is minor: the card defines patricians as 'wealthy families', but patricians were a class defined by birth, and some plebeians were also rich.
